content:
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
Data Engineering | Test & Validation Engineer (Mechanical)

 tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311 | linkedin.com/in/tfl-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design, testing and validation across automotive and industrial components. Builds Python tools to process test-rig data, validate results against specifications and generate reports, reducing report preparation from about three days to half a day per test. Uses SQL Server for trend analysis and MATLAB/Simulink for engineering models. Interested in moving into data engineering.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib) | SQL / SQL Server | MATLAB/Simulink | Excel/VBA | Power BI | LabVIEW | Minitab | ANSYS Mechanical | SolidWorks | CATIA V5 | Design of Experiments (DOE) | GD&T | DFMEA | 8D problem solving

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components — Seat structures and seat-adjuster mechanisms
Setúbal | Mar 2019–Present
- Plan and run durability, vibration and climatic tests across six servo-hydraulic and electric test rigs; prepare test reports for OEM customers.
- Developed Python scripts using pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib to read rig output files, check each channel against the test specification and generate standard report figures. Reduced report preparation time from about three days to half a day per test.
- Query the plant’s test-results database in SQL Server for trend analysis across three product generations.
- Correlate rig results with FEA in ANSYS Mechanical and lead 8D root-cause analysis on field failures. Proposed a redesigned adjuster rail bracket that reduced warranty returns for that part by 40%.
- Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive, used to select rig load profiles.

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps — Industrial centrifugal pumps
Porto | Sep 2014–Feb 2019
- Designed pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks and produced GD&T production drawings; owned DFMEA for two product lines.
- Conducted structural FEA of casings in ANSYS. Supported the change of one casing family from grey cast iron to ductile iron, saving 12% in material cost.
- Supported the conversion of the pump performance test bench to a PLC-controlled setup using Siemens S7.

EDUCATION
MSc Mechanical Engineering | Sado Valley Polytechnic | 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading

LANGUAGES
Portuguese (native) | English (fluent) | Spanish (good)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, concise, professional CV with strong quantified evidence. The Python automation achievement, 40% reduction in warranty returns, and 12% material-cost saving provide credible impact. The progression from mechanical design to test and validation is easy to follow, and the document is appropriately tailored toward a data-engineering transition without claiming unsupported cloud or platform experience. The main content limitation is that it presents engineering-data experience well but does not establish senior data-platform ownership, production operations, or data architecture experience required by this role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, chronological experience, conventional bullet points, readable dates, and no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. Relevant terms such as Python, pandas, NumPy, SQL Server, MATLAB/Simulink, data processing, trend analysis, validation, and report generation are present. AI screening probability for this specific Senior Data Engineer role is moderate to low because the document does not contain supported evidence for production data platforms, cloud data warehouses, dimensional modelling, query optimisation, Google Cloud or comparable cloud services, Airflow, dbt, Docker, CI/CD, or Git. These are substantive experience gaps rather than ATS wording problems.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with Python-based engineering data processing, SQL Server analysis, data validation, automation, reporting, and professional English. Portuguese is also clearly shown as a plus. The strongest transferable evidence is the Python pipeline that reads test-rig files, validates channels against specifications, generates reports, and reduces preparation time from about three days to half a day. However, the candidate's material does not show experience designing, building, or operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale; advanced SQL involving query optimisation on large datasets; dimensional or graph modelling; Google Cloud or a comparable cloud; or open-source/data-architecture work. The document should therefore position the candidate as an experienced engineer transitioning toward data engineering, not as an established senior data-platform engineer. No unsupported company-culture claims or technical skills have been added.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the transferable data-engineering evidence more explicit without implying platform experience. Replace the final two sentences with: "Builds Python tools that ingest test-rig output, validate channels against specifications, analyse results with SQL Server, and generate standard reports, reducing report preparation from about three days to half a day per test. Seeking to apply this experience in data engineering and data platform work." This is more directly aligned with the advert while remaining truthful.
2. In the Technical Skills section, group the existing skills under ATS-readable labels rather than one long pipe-separated line. For example: "Data and programming: Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, SQL, SQL Server, Excel/VBA, Power BI"; "Engineering and modelling: MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5"; and "Quality and methods: data validation, Design of Experiments (DOE), GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving." Only use "data validation" because the experience section explicitly supports checking every channel against the test specification.
3. In the Corvane Automotive Components experience section, move the Python automation bullet immediately after the opening test-and-validation bullet, or combine the two so the most relevant data-processing evidence appears first. In that bullet, change "read rig output files, check each channel against the test specification and generate standard report figures" to "process test-rig output files, validate each channel against the test specification, and generate standard report figures." This uses terminology closer to the role while preserving the documented work.
4. In the SQL Server bullet under Corvane Automotive Components, retain the explicit product name and make the analytical use clearer by changing it to: "Query the plant's SQL Server test-results database to perform trend analysis across three product generations." Do not describe this as query optimisation or large-scale data warehousing, since the original candidate information does not support those claims.
5. In the header, consider changing the headline from "Data Engineering | Test & Validation Engineer (Mechanical)" to "Test & Validation Engineer | Python, SQL and Engineering Data Automation." This avoids presenting data engineering as an established job function while keeping the target direction and strongest supported keywords visible to recruiters and ATS screening.

requirements.requirement: Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
Strong data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling
Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud
Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
